name: 17-bgp
description:
Three routers in a ring, each in an **autonomous system** of its own: r1 is AS 65001, r2 AS 65002 and r3 AS 65003. Each has a LAN. DockerLab gives every interface its address; the routers learn each other's LANs with **eBGP**, in FRRouting (FRR).

| Router | LAN | to the next router | to the previous router |
|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | `eth0` `192.168.1.1/24` | `eth1` `10.0.12.1/24` → r2 | `eth2` `10.0.13.1/24` → r3 |
| r2 | `eth0` `192.168.2.1/24` | `eth2` `10.0.23.2/24` → r3 | `eth1` `10.0.12.2/24` → r1 |
| r3 | `eth0` `192.168.3.1/24` | `eth2` `10.0.13.3/24` → r1 | `eth1` `10.0.23.3/24` → r2 |

pc1, pc2 and pc3 are `192.168.1.10`, `192.168.2.10` and `192.168.3.10`, on switches sw1, sw2 and sw3. Each PC's default gateway is its router's `.1`.

## Before you start
**Deploy**. The routers come up with no routing configured: from pc1, `ping -c 2 192.168.2.10` fails. Open each router's **Console** and start FRR's shell with `vtysh`.

## Configure eBGP
Each router peers with its two neighbours (on the ring links) and announces its own LAN. You can type the commands, or paste each block into the router's `vtysh` at once.

**r1** (AS 65001)
```
configure terminal
router bgp 65001
 bgp router-id 1.1.1.1
 no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
 neighbor 10.0.12.2 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 10.0.13.3 remote-as 65003
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.168.1.0/24
 exit-address-family
end
write memory
```
**r2** (AS 65002)
```
configure terminal
router bgp 65002
 bgp router-id 2.2.2.2
 no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
 neighbor 10.0.12.1 remote-as 65001
 neighbor 10.0.23.3 remote-as 65003
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.168.2.0/24
 exit-address-family
end
write memory
```
**r3** (AS 65003)
```
configure terminal
router bgp 65003
 bgp router-id 3.3.3.3
 no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
 neighbor 10.0.23.2 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 10.0.13.1 remote-as 65001
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 192.168.3.0/24
 exit-address-family
end
write memory
```

> [!NOTE]
> `no bgp ebgp-requires-policy`: by default, FRR (following RFC 8212) accepts and announces nothing on an eBGP session until a route policy allows it. Real networks set filters; this lab switches the rule off to keep the first steps short. Leave it out on r1 and watch `show bgp summary`: the session comes up, but the prefix counts say `(Policy)`.

## Verify
1. In vtysh on each router:
   ```
   show bgp summary
   show bgp ipv4 unicast
   show ip route bgp
   ```
   Two neighbours in state *Established* (a number of prefixes in the last column, not a state), and routes to the two other LANs, each with its **AS path**.
2. From pc1:
   ```
   ping -c 3 192.168.2.10
   traceroute -n 192.168.3.10
   ```
3. Capture the **r1–r2** cable: TCP port 179, with *OPEN*, *UPDATE* and *KEEPALIVE* messages.

## Go further
- [ ] On r1, look at `show bgp ipv4 unicast 192.168.3.0/24`: two paths. Which one is *best*, and why?
- [ ] **Traffic engineering with AS-path prepending.** Make r3 reach LAN 1 through r2, by making the direct path look longer:
  ```
  configure terminal
  route-map PREPEND permit 10
   set as-path prepend 65001 65001
  exit
  router bgp 65001
   address-family ipv4 unicast
    neighbor 10.0.13.3 route-map PREPEND out
  end
  clear bgp 10.0.13.3 soft out
  ```
  On r3, `show bgp ipv4 unicast 192.168.1.0/24`: which path is best now? Does traffic from pc3 to pc1 take r2 (`traceroute -n 192.168.1.10` on pc3)? And the replies?
- [ ] Take the r1–r3 link down from r1's console (not vtysh): `ip link set eth2 down`. How quickly does r1 move to the path through r2? Then `ip link set eth2 up`.

## Questions
- [ ] OSPF (lab 11) chose paths by cost. What does BGP compare first here?
- [ ] Why does r1 not accept a route whose AS path already contains 65001?
- [ ] Each router announces only its LAN. Why can pc1 still ping r2's address `10.0.23.2`, or can it?

nodes.name: pc1
nodes.startup:
# r1 is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.1.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

nodes.name: pc2
nodes.startup:
# r2 is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.2.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

nodes.name: pc3
nodes.startup:
# r3 is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.3.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

images.dockerlab/host:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Everyday tools for an end host: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
images.dockerlab/frr:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# FRRouting (vtysh, zebra, staticd, ospfd, ripd, bgpd), plus the network tools
RUN apk add --no-cache frr iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils

# Turn on the routing protocol daemons the labs use (zebra and staticd always run)
RUN sed -i -e 's/^ospfd=no/ospfd=yes/' -e 's/^ripd=no/ripd=yes/' -e 's/^bgpd=no/bgpd=yes/' /etc/frr/daemons

# Start FRR with the container; its configuration is /etc/frr/frr.conf (vtysh: write memory)
CMD ["sh", "-c", "/usr/lib/frr/frrinit.sh start; exec sleep infinity"]
